card.intuition: A spec is a handoff artifact describing multi-session work — what is being built, not how each session does its share — and it mutates as work progresses. It is made of tickets and exists because sessions are disposable while big work is not: any fresh session reads the spec to know where the work stands without inheriting the previous session's noise. It comes in styles like PRD, design doc, or a plain plan.md, which matter less than the role it plays.
card.analogy: A construction bluebook: the charter states the building's intent and the milestone list, and each day's fresh crew reads it instead of inheriting yesterday's confusion.
card.time_complexity: The model is stateless, so re-reading the spec into a new session costs tokens on every request, but much less than inheriting a full noisy session.
card.space_complexity: The spec lives outside the context window in the environment, so it survives clearing and a fresh session loads only what it needs.
when_to_use: For work spanning more than one context window of effort
Enumerating work as tickets so each one can run in its own session
Keeping a durable statement of intent that each session reads at its start
Avoiding the dumb zone by splitting work before a single context overloads
gotchas: Sessions are disposable — without a spec, multi-session work has no home and dies on clearing
A spec describes what and why, not per-session how — keep session-specific steps out of it
Style matters less than role: a fresh session must be able to read it cold at the start

steps.label: Big work
steps.annotation: Work bigger than one context window needs a home outside the context.

steps.label: Write spec
steps.annotation: The spec records the goal, the constraints, and the decisions made so far along with the ticket list and status.

steps.label: Break into tickets
steps.annotation: Work is broken into tickets, each small enough to be completed within a single session.

steps.label: Seed each session
steps.annotation: Every fresh session starts by reading the durable statement of intent held in the spec.

steps.label: Mutates as work progresses
steps.annotation: The spec is updated as work moves, so any session entering later knows exactly where things stand.

exercise.prompt: Complete seed_session so it adds a freshly opened ticket to the spec and returns that ticket as the brief for the next session.
hints: A spec is the durable statement of intent that a fresh session reads first.
Each ticket in the spec is scoped to one session of work.
exercise.test_code:
spec = {'tickets': []}
t = seed_session(spec, 'A')
assert spec['tickets'] == [{'id': 'A', 'status': 'open'}]
assert t['status'] == 'open'
print('PASS')
